questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Kabul?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Afghanistan is Kabul.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Afghanistan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Afghanistan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Afghanistan about 652,230 square kilometres; Syria about 185,180 square kilometres; Greece about 131,957 square kilometres; Bulgaria about 110,994 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Afghanistan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Afghanistan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Afghanistan article.

questions.proof: It borders Pakistan in the south and east (border with India is disputed), Iran in the west, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the north, and China in the far northeast.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Afghanistan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Afghanistan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
